action.name: Queued: the place in line is the run's output

description: Fires once per PR head SHA when its checks settle not green (a head with no counted check, conclusion no_checks, is left alone; so is a head GitGuardian fails on, d25: pr-fixer-secrets reports it and a human acts). Same-repo, non-draft PRs of repos in vars.fixer_repos only; vars.fixer_excluded_repos overrides it. Adds the PR to the fixer queue (#35, d29: workflow queue-add); pr-fixer-dispatch starts its pr-fix run when it reaches the head of the line. Shares the per-PR concurrency key with the other pr-fixer-* rules (so a human push still resets the PR's attempt budget) but is not an attempt itself. Only while the PR is open.
name: PR fixer: checks settled

on_failure.name: Hand back with the run link (once per chain)

params.body: PR fixer handed back ({{ run.error.code }}): {{ run.error.message }}

inputs.instruction: Checks on PR {{ trigger.data.repository }}#{{ trigger.data.number }} settled ({{ trigger.data.conclusion }}) at {{ trigger.data.head_sha }}. Work on the PR head branch {{ trigger.data.head_branch }} only. Fix the failing checks and the SonarCloud issues behind the failing quality gate, and address the review threads in the threads input (and no other thread). Never edit .github/workflows, never delete or skip tests and never add suppression markers. In threads_addressed, use each thread's thread_id exactly as the threads input gives it. For SonarCloud, follow sonar_note: when the quality gate fails, the sonar_issues input lists only the issues behind the failing conditions: fix exactly those; when the gate passes, it lists the issues on this PR's own new code: fix a listed new-code issue only if the trusted request names it. Never the rest of the Sonar backlog.
